passages.text: “Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees who were with Him.
He said, “I tell you the truth.
Anyone who does not enter the sheepfold by the gate is not acting rightly.
If someone climbs in by another way, that person is a thief.
That person is also a robber.”
passages.original: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὁ μὴ εἰσερχόμενος διὰ τῆς θύρας εἰς τὴν αὐλὴν τῶν προβάτων ἀλλὰ ἀναβαίνων ἀλλαχόθεν ἐκεῖνος κλέπτης ἐστὶν καὶ λῃστής

passages.text: But the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
passages.sermon:
The shepherd cares for the sheep.
The shepherd enters the sheepfold through the gate.
The person who enters by the gate is the shepherd.
The shepherd belongs to the sheep.
The shepherd does not sneak in another way.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ εἰσερχόμενος διὰ τῆς θύρας ποιμήν ἐστιν τῶν προβάτων

passages.text: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen for his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
passages.sermon:
The shepherd enters by the gate.
The gatekeeper opens the gate for the shepherd.
The sheep listen for the shepherd’s voice.
The shepherd calls his own sheep by name.
The shepherd leads his own sheep out.
passages.original: τούτῳ ὁ θυρωρὸς ἀνοίγει καὶ τὰ πρόβατα τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούει καὶ τὰ ἴδια πρόβατα φωνεῖ κατ’ ὄνομα καὶ ἐξάγει αὐτά

passages.text: When he has brought out all his own, he goes on ahead of them, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.
passages.sermon:
The shepherd brings out all his own sheep.
He goes ahead of them.
The sheep follow him.
They know his voice.
passages.original: Ὅταν τὰ ἴδια πάντα ἐκβάλῃ ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν πορεύεται καὶ τὰ πρόβατα αὐτῷ ἀκολουθεῖ ὅτι οἴδασιν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But they will never follow a stranger; in fact, they will flee from him because they do not recognize his voice.”
passages.sermon: The sheep do not follow a stranger.\r\nThey run away from a stranger.\r\nThey do this because they do not know the stranger’s voice.
passages.original: ἀλλοτρίῳ δὲ οὐ μὴ ἀκολουθήσουσιν ἀλλὰ φεύξονται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὐκ οἴδασιν τῶν ἀλλοτρίων τὴν φωνήν

passages.text: Jesus spoke to them using this illustration, but they did not understand what He was telling them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He used an illustration.
The people did not understand Him.
They did not know what He was telling them.
passages.original: Ταύτην τὴν παροιμίαν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οὐκ ἔγνωσαν τίνα ἦν ἃ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς

passages.text: So He said to them again, “Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the gate for the sheep.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people again.
Jesus is the speaker.
Jesus said, “Truly, truly, I tell you.
I am the gate for the sheep.
The sheep must go through the gate.
I am that gate.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν οὖν πάλιν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα τῶν προβάτων

passages.text: All who came before Me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nHe said, "All who came before Me were thieves and robbers.\r\nThe sheep did not listen to them."
passages.original: πάντες ὅσοι ἦλθον πρὸ ἐμοῦ κλέπται εἰσὶν καὶ λῃσταί ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἤκουσαν αὐτῶν τὰ πρόβατα

passages.text: I am the gate. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved. He will come in and go out and find pasture.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, “I am the gate for the sheep.”
If anyone enters through Me, that person will be saved.
That person will come in.
That person will go out.
That person will find pasture.
passages.original: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ θύρα δι’ ἐμοῦ ἐάν τις εἰσέλθῃ σωθήσεται καὶ εἰσελεύσεται καὶ ἐξελεύσεται καὶ νομὴν εὑρήσει

passages.text: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.
passages.sermon:
The thief comes only to steal.
The thief comes only to kill.
The thief comes only to destroy.
I have come so that people may have life.
I have come so that people may have life in all its fullness.
passages.original: ὁ κλέπτης οὐκ ἔρχεται εἰ μὴ ἵνα κλέψῃ καὶ θύσῃ καὶ ἀπολέσῃ ἐγὼ ἦλθον ἵνα ζωὴν ἔχωσιν καὶ περισσὸν ἔχωσιν

passages.text: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
passages.sermon: Jesus is the good shepherd.\r\nThe good shepherd gives his life for the sheep.
passages.original: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλὸς τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ τίθησιν ὑπὲρ τῶν προβάτων

passages.text: The hired hand is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. When he sees the wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf pounces on them and scatters the flock.
passages.sermon:
The hired hand is not the shepherd.
The sheep do not belong to him.
He sees the wolf coming.
He leaves the sheep.
He runs away.
The wolf attacks the sheep.
The wolf scatters the flock.
passages.original: ὁ μισθωτὸς καὶ οὐκ ὢν ποιμήν οὗ οὐκ ἔστιν τὰ πρόβατα ἴδια θεωρεῖ τὸν λύκον ἐρχόμενον καὶ ἀφίησιν τὰ πρόβατα καὶ φεύγει καὶ ὁ λύκος ἁρπάζει αὐτὰ καὶ σκορπίζει

passages.text: The man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep.
passages.sermon:
The man is a hired servant.
He does not own the sheep.
He does not care about the sheep.
He runs away when danger comes.
passages.original: ὅτι μισθωτός ἐστιν καὶ οὐ μέλει αὐτῷ περὶ τῶν προβάτων

passages.text: I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep and My sheep know Me, just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father. And I lay down My life for the sheep.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the good shepherd.
He knows His sheep.
His sheep know Him.
The Father knows Jesus.
Jesus knows the Father.
Jesus lays down His life for the sheep.
passages.original: Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός καὶ γινώσκω τὰ ἐμὰ καὶ γινώσκουσί με τὰ ἐμά καθὼς γινώσκει με ὁ Πατὴρ κἀγὼ γινώσκω τὸν Πατέρα καὶ τὴν ψυχήν μου τίθημι ὑπὲρ τῶν προβάτων

passages.text: I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the good shepherd.
Jesus has sheep.
Some of Jesus’ sheep are not in this sheepfold.
Jesus must bring these other sheep also.
These other sheep will listen to Jesus’ voice.
All the sheep will become one flock.
There will be one shepherd for this flock.
passages.original: καὶ ἄλλα πρόβατα ἔχω ἃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τῆς αὐλῆς ταύτης κἀκεῖνα δεῖ με ἀγαγεῖν καὶ τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσουσιν καὶ γενήσονται μία ποίμνη εἷς ποιμήν

passages.text: The reason the Father loves Me is that I lay down My life in order to take it up again.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
The Father loves Jesus.
The Father loves Jesus because Jesus lays down His life.
Jesus lays down His life so that He may take it up again.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτό με ὁ Πατὴρ ἀγαπᾷ ὅτι ἐγὼ τίθημι τὴν ψυχήν μου ἵνα πάλιν λάβω αὐτήν

passages.text: No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord. I have authority to lay it down and authority to take it up again. This charge I have received from My Father.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking about His own life.
No one takes Jesus’ life from Him.
Jesus lays down His life by His own choice.
Jesus has authority to lay down His life.
Jesus also has authority to take up His life again.
Jesus received this command from His Father.
passages.original: οὐδεὶς αἴρει αὐτὴν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ τίθημι αὐτὴν ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω θεῖναι αὐτήν καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔχω πάλιν λαβεῖν αὐτήν ταύτην τὴν ἐντολὴν ἔλαβον παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός μου

passages.text: Again there was division among the Jews because of Jesus’ message.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke a message to the people.
Many Jews heard His words.
His message caused disagreement among them.
The Jews became divided again because of what Jesus said.
passages.original: Σχίσμα πάλιν ἐγένετο ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις διὰ τοὺς λόγους τούτους

passages.text: Many of them said, “He is demon-possessed and insane. Why would you listen to Him?”
passages.sermon:
Many Jews heard Jesus speak.
Many of these Jews spoke to each other.
They said, “He has a demon.”
They said, “He is insane.”
They asked, “Why do you listen to Him?”
passages.original: ἔλεγον δὲ πολλοὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν Δαιμόνιον ἔχει καὶ μαίνεται τί αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε

passages.text: But others replied, “These are not the words of a man possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”
passages.sermon:
Some people disagreed with the others.
They spoke about Jesus.
They said, “These words do not come from a man with a demon.”
They asked, “Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”
passages.original: Ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα οὐκ ἔστιν δαιμονιζομένου μὴ δαιμόνιον δύναται τυφλῶν ὀφθαλμοὺς ἀνοῖξαι

passages.text: At that time the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem. It was winter, and Jesus was walking in the temple courts in Solomon’s Colonnade.
passages.sermon:
The Feast of Dedication happened in Jerusalem at that time.
It was winter.
Jesus walked in the temple courts.
He walked in Solomon’s Colonnade.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο τότε τὰ ἐνκαίνια ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις χειμὼν ἦν καὶ περιεπάτει ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐν τῇ στοᾷ τοῦ Σολομῶνος

passages.text: So the Jews gathered around Him and demanded, “How long will You keep us in suspense? If You are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
passages.sermon:
The Jews gathered around Jesus.
They spoke to Him.
They said, “How long will You keep us in suspense?”
They asked, “If You are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
passages.original: ἐκύκλωσαν οὖν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῷ Ἕως πότε τὴν ψυχὴν ἡμῶν αἴρεις εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστός εἰπὲ ἡμῖν παρρησίᾳ

passages.text: “I already told you,” Jesus replied, “but you did not believe. The works I do in My Father’s name testify on My behalf.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus had already told them who He was.
They did not believe Him.
Jesus did works in His Father's name.
These works showed who Jesus was.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Εἶπον ὑμῖν καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε τὰ ἔργα ἃ ἐγὼ ποιῶ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Πατρός μου ταῦτα μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: But because you are not My sheep, you refuse to believe.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews who gathered around Him.
He said, "You do not believe.
You are not My sheep.
That is why you do not believe."
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετε ὅτι οὐκ ἐστὲ ἐκ τῶν προβάτων τῶν ἐμῶν

passages.text: My sheep listen to My voice; I know them, and they follow Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about His followers.
His followers are like sheep.
My sheep listen to My voice.
I know My sheep.
My sheep follow Me.
passages.original: τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἐμὰ τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούουσιν κἀγὼ γινώσκω αὐτά καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσίν μοι

passages.text: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks about His sheep.
He gives His sheep eternal life.
His sheep will never perish.
No one can snatch His sheep out of His hand.
passages.original: κἀγὼ δίδωμι αὐτοῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀπόλωνται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα καὶ οὐχ ἁρπάσει τις αὐτὰ ἐκ τῆς χειρός μου

passages.text: My Father who has given them to Me is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of My Father’s hand.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father of Jesus.
The Father gave the sheep to Jesus.
The Father is greater than everyone.
No one can take the sheep from the Father's hand.
passages.original: ὁ Πατήρ μου ὃ δέδωκέν μοι πάντων μεῖζόν ἐστιν καὶ οὐδεὶς δύναται ἁρπάζειν ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ Πατρός

passages.text: I and the Father are one.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, “I and the Father are one.”
Jesus claimed unity with God the Father.
Jesus declared that He and God share the same nature.
passages.original: ἐγὼ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἕν ἐσμεν

passages.text: At this, the Jews again picked up stones to stone Him.
passages.sermon:
The Jews heard Jesus speak.
They became angry.
They picked up stones.
They wanted to stone Jesus again.
passages.original: Ἐβάστασαν οὖν πάλιν λίθους οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἵνα λιθάσωσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: But Jesus responded, “I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of these do you stone Me?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus had performed many good works.
These good works came from the Father.
Jesus asked them a question.
He said, "For which of these good works do you stone Me?"
passages.original: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πολλὰ ἔργα ἔδειξα ὑμῖν καλὰ ἐκ τοῦ Πατρός διὰ ποῖον αὐτῶν ἔργον ἐμὲ λιθάζετε

passages.text: “We are not stoning You for any good work,” said the Jews, “but for blasphemy, because You, who are a man, declare Yourself to be God.”
passages.sermon:
The Jews answered Jesus.
They said, “We are not stoning you for any good work.
We are stoning you for blasphemy.
You are a man.
You make yourself God.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι Περὶ καλοῦ ἔργου οὐ λιθάζομέν σε ἀλλὰ περὶ βλασφημίας καὶ ὅτι σὺ ἄνθρωπος ὢν ποιεῖς σεαυτὸν Θεόν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “Is it not written in your Law: ‘I have said you are gods’?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews.
He answered their accusation.
He referred to their Law.
He said, “Is it not written in your Law?”
He quoted, “I have said you are gods.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐκ ἔστιν γεγραμμένον ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ὑμῶν ὅτι Ἐγὼ εἶπα Θεοί ἐστε

passages.text: If he called them gods to whom the word of God came—and the Scripture cannot be broken— then what about the One whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world? How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am the Son of God?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews.
Jesus referred to people who received the word of God.
Scripture called these people "gods."
Scripture cannot be broken.
God the Father set apart one person.
God the Father sent this person into the world.
This person is Jesus.
Jesus said, "I am the Son of God."
The Jews accused Jesus of blasphemy for this claim.
Jesus questioned their accusation.
Jesus asked why they called Him a blasphemer for saying He is the Son of God.
Jesus pointed out that Scripture used the word "gods" for others.
Jesus showed that His claim is not blasphemy.
passages.original: εἰ ἐκείνους εἶπεν θεοὺς πρὸς οὓς ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐγένετο καὶ οὐ δύναται λυθῆναι ἡ γραφή ὃν ὁ Πατὴρ ἡγίασεν καὶ ἀπέστειλεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Βλασφημεῖς ὅτι εἶπον Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰμι

passages.text: If I am not doing the works of My Father, then do not believe Me.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nJesus is the Son of God.\r\nJesus said, "If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me."
passages.original: Εἰ οὐ ποιῶ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ Πατρός μου μὴ πιστεύετέ μοι

passages.text: But if I am doing them, even though you do not believe Me, believe the works themselves, so that you may know and understand that the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to the people.
\r\nJesus does the works of God the Father.
\r\nSome people do not believe Jesus.
\r\nJesus tells them to look at His works.
\r\nJesus says, "If you do not believe Me, believe the works I do."
\r\nThe works show who Jesus is.
\r\nThe works help people know the truth.
\r\nThe works help people understand that the Father is in Jesus.
\r\nThe works show that Jesus is in the Father.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ ποιῶ κἂν ἐμοὶ μὴ πιστεύητε τοῖς ἔργοις πιστεύετε ἵνα γνῶτε καὶ γινώσκητε ὅτι ἐν ἐμοὶ ὁ Πατὴρ κἀγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρί

passages.text: At this, they tried again to seize Him, but He escaped their grasp.
passages.sermon: The people tried again to seize Jesus.\r\nJesus escaped from their grasp.
passages.original: Ἐζήτουν οὖν αὐτὸν πάλιν πιάσαι καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν

passages.text: Then Jesus went back across the Jordan to the place where John had first been baptizing, and He stayed there.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left the place where He was.
He went across the Jordan River.
He went to the place where John had first baptized people.
Jesus stayed there.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πάλιν πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου εἰς τὸν τόπον ὅπου ἦν Ἰωάννης τὸ πρῶτον βαπτίζων καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ

passages.text: Many came to Him and said, “Although John never performed a sign, everything he said about this man was true.”
passages.sermon:
Many people came to Jesus.
They spoke to Him.
They said that John did not perform any sign.
They said that everything John said about Jesus was true.
passages.original: καὶ πολλοὶ ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάννης μὲν σημεῖον ἐποίησεν οὐδέν πάντα δὲ ὅσα εἶπεν Ἰωάννης περὶ τούτου ἀληθῆ ἦν

passages.text: And many in that place believed in Jesus.
passages.sermon: Many people were in that place.\r\nThey believed in Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν ἐκεῖ
